name: Content Summary
description: Turn a video, podcast, lecture, interview, or narration transcript into a structured content brief.
prompt: Create a self-contained content brief for someone who has not seen or heard the source. Preserve the source's central subject, reasoning, evidence, examples, terminology, caveats, conclusions, and meaningful changes of viewpoint according to the selected detail level. Separate what the source explicitly claims from examples, speculation, or unanswered questions. Remove greetings, sponsorships, repeated phrasing, filler, and calls to action unless they are part of the substantive content. Do not describe the source as a meeting, do not address the user, and never ask how the transcript should be processed.

sections.title: Overview
sections.instruction: Explain what the source is about, why it matters, its purpose, and its main conclusion or takeaway in a compact opening

sections.title: Core Ideas
sections.instruction: Present the most important claims, explanations, techniques, events, or lessons in a logical order. Preserve causal relationships and distinguish the source's position from cited or opposing views

sections.title: Evidence & Important Details
sections.instruction: Capture the concrete examples, evidence, mechanisms, comparisons, numbers, names, definitions, or caveats needed to understand and evaluate the core ideas

sections.title: Practical Takeaways
sections.instruction: List methods, recommendations, lessons, or implications that a reader can apply. Keep descriptive content descriptive; do not manufacture advice when the source provides none

sections.title: Conclusions & Open Questions
sections.instruction: State the source's conclusions, qualifications, unresolved questions, or intended takeaway without adding outside opinions

sections.title: Keywords
sections.instruction: List 5 to 12 precise keywords or named concepts useful for searching and categorizing this content
